<objective>
Replace `CategoryService`'s deferred, untyped lookup of `IndexedDBUserModelService` with ordinary constructor injection.

Framing matters here, and the roadmap's wording is imprecise. Research traced the full import chain and found that `IndexedDBUserModelService` never references `CategoryService` — it injects only `NativeIndexedDBService`, which knows nothing about categories. There is no class-level dependency cycle in the codebase today. The deferred-lookup scaffolding has been present since `category.service.ts`'s very first commit and appears anticipatory rather than a remedy for an encountered runtime injector error.

So this is the removal of an unnecessary indirection, not the breaking of a cycle. The observable end state that satisfies the roadmap's success criterion is identical either way: a typed constructor parameter, no runtime lookup, no untyped field. The real risk being retired is that the original motivation is unproven, so this plan carries an explicit verification that the injector graph still constructs.

Purpose: restore compile-time type safety on the cascade-update call path and delete an async indirection from every cascade operation.
Output: a simplified `CategoryService` constructor and cascade path, plus evidence that nothing depended on the deferred behaviour.
</objective>

  <action>
Before changing anything, confirm the no-cycle premise yourself rather than trusting it: search `indexeddb-user-model.service.ts`, `native-indexeddb.service.ts`, and `indexeddb-config.ts` for any reference to the category service. If you find one, stop and report it — the premise of this task would be wrong and the plan would need revision. Record the result of this check in the plan summary either way.

Then make four coordinated edits.

Import line: drop the injector symbol from the `@angular/core` import, leaving only `Injectable`. Add `IndexedDBUserModelService` from `./indexeddb-user-model.service`, grouped with the other local-service imports and kept alphabetically ordered within that group per the repo's import convention.

Field: delete the untyped lazily-populated field declared just above the constructor at line 68, together with its trailing comment about avoiding a circular dependency. Do not replace it with a differently-named cache field — the injected parameter is the cache.

Constructor: replace the second parameter with a typed `private userModelService: IndexedDBUserModelService`. Keep the first parameter and the `initPromise` assignment in the body exactly as they are.

Cascade path: in `cascadeRenameCategory`, delete the awaited lookup call and the guard block that logs a warning and returns early when the lookup yielded nothing. That branch becomes unreachable dead code — a constructor-injected dependency cannot be absent, and leaving it would imply a failure mode that no longer exists. Change the two call sites that read `getAllUserModels()` and `updateUserModel(...)` to go through the injected member. Leave the type-discrimination filter, the per-model try/catch, and the error logging inside the loop byte-for-byte unchanged; the spec from plan 02-01 pins that behaviour and any alteration will be caught. `cascadeDeleteCategory` delegates to `cascadeRenameCategory` and needs no change.

Lookup helper: delete the entire private async helper method at lines 441-457 along with its JSDoc block.

Do not use `forwardRef` or an injection-token indirection. Angular's own guidance scopes `forwardRef` to circular component imports rather than service-to-service graphs, and there is no cycle here to work around in any case.

Do not modify `category.service.spec.ts` in this task. Its value as a safety net comes from passing unmodified across the change.

Leave no comment in `category.service.ts` naming the removed symbols or narrating the removal. Git history records what was removed; a lingering comment referencing a deleted helper is exactly the kind of stale breadcrumb the acceptance greps below are checking for.
  </action>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| category rename/delete UI → persisted user-model records | A cascade operation rewrites the `category` field of stored user models. Widening the filter would rewrite records the user did not intend to touch. |

|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|

Task 2's production build plus full-suite scan for `NG0200` and `Circular dependency` is the explicit gate; a hit stops the plan rather than being patched over with `forwardRef`. |
| T-02-09 | Repudiation | `cascadeRenameCategory` silent early-return | low | mitigate | The removed guard could swallow an entire cascade with only a console warning, leaving records silently unmigrated. Direct injection removes the failure mode; Task 2's empty-list spec confirms the remaining path reports correctly. |
